:::{#def-quasipoisson}
#### Quasipoisson regression

**Quasipoisson regression** assumes the Poisson regression mean function
$\E{Y \mid \vX = \vx, T = t} = \mu(\vx, t) \eqdef t \expf{\eta(\vx)}$
and the variance function

$$\Var{Y \mid \vX = \vx, T = t} = \theta \, \mu(\vx, t)$$

for a dispersion parameter $\theta > 0$,
without assuming a full distribution for $Y$.
It estimates $\vb$ with the Poisson regression estimate $\evb$,
and estimates $\theta$ by the
[Pearson $\chi^2$ statistic](Intro-to-GLMs.qmd#def-pearson-chisq-glm)
divided by its residual degrees of freedom:

$$
\eth \eqdef \frac{1}{n - (p + 1)} \sumin \frac{(y_i - \emu_i)^2}{\emu_i}
$$ {#eq-quasipoisson-theta}

where $n$ is the number of observations
and $p + 1$ is the number of estimated coefficients
(an intercept and $p$ covariate coefficients).
The quasipoisson standard error of each $\eb_j$
is the Poisson regression standard error multiplied by $\sqrt{\eth}$.

:::
